newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends higher on late local rally.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends higher on late local rally.

text.p: CSCE world sugar ended slightly higher on a local-driven short-covering rally, after testing support at 11.50 cents a lb in the October contract.
"Locals dominated the activity most of the day," said one commission house broker. "The trade started it off at the lower end of the range and the locals did some buying on the close."
The October delivery contract ended at 11.61 cents a lb, up 0.03 cents from Monday, in a range of 11.50 to 11.64 cents a lb.

Brazilian producers are believed to be consistant hedge sellers since the removal of export quotas. "That's what seems to be capping any rally we have," said Judith Ganes, an analyst with Merrill Lynch & Co.

"The Brazilian exports should offset any shortage from the Thai crop," she said, referring to a recent ED&F Man report that final sugar output would decline in 1997/98 to 5.07 million tonnes from 5.8 million tonnes this year.
